topic: Present Perfect Continuous vs Past Simple
intro: Covers choosing and forming Present Perfect Continuous and Past Simple in context

items.q: She ___ for three hours and she still isn't finished.
items.why: Ongoing activity with duration up to now needs Present Perfect Continuous.

items.q: I ___ my keys this morning and had to call a locksmith.
items.why: Completed event at a specific past time needs Past Simple.

items.q: Why are your shoes wet? ___ you been walking in the rain?
items.why: Recent activity with present evidence uses Present Perfect Continuous.

items.q: How long ___ you been waiting for the bus?
items.why: Duration of an activity continuing up to now uses Present Perfect Continuous.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.post: on that engine since early morning.
items.why: Activity in progress from a past point up to now.

items.post: the report an hour ago and sent it to my manager.
items.why: Completed action at a specific past time uses Past Simple.

items.pre: Your eyes are red. How long
items.why: Asking about duration of a recent emotional activity.

items.post: the living room all weekend, so we're exhausted now.
items.why: Recent prolonged activity explaining a present result.

items.post: well last night because of the noise from next door.
items.why: Specific completed past period uses Past Simple negative.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: I have been seeing that film last Saturday with my friend.
items.corrected: I saw that film last Saturday with my friend.
items.why: Specific past time expression requires Past Simple, not Perfect Continuous.

items.sentence: She works in the garden all afternoon and now she's really tired.
items.corrected: She has been working in the garden all afternoon and now she's really tired.
items.why: Activity with present result and duration needs Present Perfect Continuous.

items.sentence: How long did you been learning English?
items.corrected: How long have you been learning English?
items.why: Duration up to now uses 'have' not 'did' in Present Perfect Continuous.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Describe something you started doing recently and are still doing now. Say how long you have been doing it.
items.criteria: Accept Present Perfect Continuous with a time expression, e.g. 'for' or 'since'.
items.example: I have been learning to cook for the past few weeks and I really enjoy it.

items.prompt: Describe something you did at a specific time in the past that is now completely finished.
items.criteria: Accept Past Simple with a clear past time reference or finished context.
items.example: I visited my grandmother last weekend and we had a lovely dinner together.
